sections.html:
Limestone County fills the top of Alabama against the Tennessee line, with Athens as its seat. It belongs to the Huntsville metro area, so jobs and prices in Huntsville spill over here. Population climbed about 25% in the ten years to 2020, when 103,570 people were counted, and the latest estimate is 122,928.

The county has 42,692 housing units, of which 7.8% stood empty at the last count, and owners live in 76.5% of the occupied ones. A typical sale is a single-family house with an owner behind it. Rural living is common, with about half the population outside towns, so expect acreage and a longer drive to shopping to enter a buyer's math.

Both the Elk and Tennessee rivers run through the county. Lenders sometimes raise extra questions about land near water, which a cash purchase never faces.

Athens, home to 25,406 people in 2020, is the biggest city wholly within county lines. Madison and Huntsville extend into it though they belong mostly to Madison County, and Decatur does the same from Morgan County. Ardmore, Elkmont, Lester and Mooresville are towns, while Belle Mina, Capshaw, Tanner, Veto and Greenbrier have no municipal government.

Students are served by five systems: Limestone County Schools across most of the rural area, plus Athens, Decatur, Huntsville and Madison city schools. Bills add up state, county, city and school levies, so an Athens house and a country house are billed differently. Look at the exact parcel instead of assuming a neighbor's bill applies to yours.

Buyers care about access to Interstates 65 and 565 and U.S. 31 and U.S. 72, so name the closest interchange when you describe the house.

sections.h2: Due dates and the online portal
sections.html:
Here the statewide calendar applies. October 1 is the due date, and the year's end brings delinquency. In February the account is handed to probate court, notices appear in the newspaper in April, and a sale is held in May.

At limestonerevenue.net the Revenue Commissioner offers a Citizen Access Portal covering real estate and business personal property. Look up your parcel there to see the number, owner and bill, then call the office if you need a payoff.

Three places hold parts of your record: the Revenue Commissioner, the probate office and the title company. Direct each question to the right one.

A homestead exemption is the principal way to lower a bill. The home must be a single-family, owner-occupied primary residence on up to 160 acres as of the first day of the tax year. Apply at the county office.

  • Under age 65, an owner may take up to $4,000 of assessed value off state tax and, in the usual case, $2,000 off county tax.
  • Low-income owners 65 and older may qualify for broader relief, and an owner who is permanently and totally disabled can qualify at any age.
  • Blind owners can qualify at any age for state-level relief.

An exemption is tied to the resident, not the house. Your buyer will not get yours, and heirs who keep the property must file separately.

Value disputes go first to the county Board of Equalization. Because the filing window follows the date new values are announced, call the Revenue Commissioner each year for exact dates.

When the board will not change the value, section 40-3-25 points to circuit court. File within 30 days after the board's final decision, notify the board secretary and circuit clerk, and post a bond for costs. A jury request is allowed within 10 days. Whoever loses can go on to the Alabama Supreme Court within 42 days of the circuit judgment.

The prior year's tax must have been paid on time, or bonded, or the appeal cannot go forward. Limestone County makes up the 39th Judicial Circuit.

Whoever buys at a tax sale does not take final title immediately. Section 40-10-120 lets the owner, heirs, personal representatives, a mortgagee or any person with a legal or equitable interest buy the property back. A portion of the land sold may be redeemed alone.

Who redeemsTime allowed
Owner, heirs or other interested partyThree years after the sale
Recorded mortgage holderOne more year, counted from the purchaser's written notice
Minor or incapacitated personOne year after the disability ends

For an owner whose house went at a tax sale, the three-year window is the deadline that counts. A seller in that position should know that the open sale becomes the buyer's problem at closing, so collect the facts from the Revenue Commissioner before settling on a price.

Owing tax does not block a sale. The title company obtains the payoff from the Revenue Commissioner and subtracts it from your proceeds. Have that number in hand before accepting an offer, because it tells you what you will really net.

Try to finish before the May sale. After a parcel is sold, the redemption period starts to matter and the closing must account for it.

Expect the process to run in a set order. The title company opens an order, runs the search, requests the payoff and sends you a draft settlement statement. Read that statement line by line. The tax line should match the payoff you were quoted, and any difference is worth a phone call before closing day, not after.

Keep the paid receipt once the tax is cleared, because it is the simplest proof that the account is current., and a buyer's title agent may ask to see it.

Start with the parcel number from the portal and your recorded deed. Print the bill and any receipt for the last payment. If anyone besides you holds an interest in the property, such as a co-owner or an heir, learn their names and contact details early, because every one of them may have to sign.

Then ask the Revenue Commissioner whether the parcel carries any open balance and whether it was ever sold at tax sale. A short call settles it, and the answer tells a buyer whether the title is clean.

sections.h2: Common situations for Limestone County sellers
sections.html:
Three situations come up most: inherited houses, rural acreage with an older home, and rentals whose owners are tired of managing them. After an inheritance, list every heir and confirm the deed history. For acreage, learn where your boundaries run and which buildings appear on the record.

Cash Home Buyers makes offers on Limestone County houses in each case, even where a tax sale is open, and will go over the numbers with you before you commit to anything. With no lender appraisal or repair list in the way, you choose the closing date, limited only by how long the title work takes.

faqs.q: Which office handles Limestone County property tax?
faqs.a: The Revenue Commissioner, in the county seat of Athens, also keeps a public lookup portal at limestonerevenue.net.

faqs.q: When are Limestone County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The due date is October 1, and unpaid bills turn delinquent when the year ends.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem a Limestone County house after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Usually three years from the sale date, per section 40-10-120. Certain lienholders and people with a legal disability are allowed more time.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal to circuit court?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the Board of Equalization's final decision, under section 40-3-25, and the taxes must be paid or bonded for the appeal to continue.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Limestone County house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing proceeds pay the balance. Get a current payoff from the Revenue Commissioner before settling on a price.
